sb_prompt: WHY DO YOU THINK THAT ONLY ABOUT HALF OF ELIGIBLE VOTERS IN AMERICA TAKE PART IN NATIONAL ELECTIONS
turns: Yeah, hello there. You know, I was just thinking about that thing we got in the mail about voting... it really does seem like half the people don't bother, doesn't it?
Yeah, that's what I was thinking, I mean it's just strange.

It's just... I know my sister, she's pretty smart, and she never votes. It's like she thinks her one vote doesn't matter, but then she gets mad when things don't go her way, so I don't know what to tell her.

Yeah, it is weird. My brother-in-law is the same way. He'll sit around and complain about the President or the Congress like nothing is his fault, but then when we ask him to go to the polls on Election Day, he says, "Why bother? Nobody listens anyway.
Yeah, but I guess it's different for her because she actually works in an office where she sees how things get decided, so maybe she just feels powerless even though she knows how the system works.
Yeah, that's probably it, but still, it just feels like everyone else does it too, so why should I be the one to make the difference?

Yeah, but then again, I don't know if that's actually true for everyone, you know? My cousin went to the polls last week and showed up to yell at the guy running the booth because they were too slow, even though he was the one who didn't vote.
Yeah, but that's just your cousin being annoying, isn't he? I don't think he's right about why I don't vote. I've just never felt like my voice would actually change anything.
Right, but you know, it's just that weird feeling of thinking the system is rigged, and then you don't want to play the game if everyone else isn't playing either.
Yeah, I guess that's what it is for me, I just didn't feel like my vote mattered years ago and I never really figured out why I stopped caring in the first place.

Yeah, but it's just frustrating because you know your sister sees the stuff in the office—the committees, the budget meetings—and she knows people are actually deciding things, so why does she feel like her vote is worthless? It's like she knows the answer but still won't do the part she's supposed to do.

Yeah, but I've been in real estate long enough to know that most people don't even read the disclosure forms, so I guess if they don't ask the questions while they're buying a house, they won't bother asking them when they vote either.

Yeah, I mean, it's just that... if nobody's reading the forms, then maybe we're all just leaving ourselves open to getting screwed over, which is scary, but at the same time, knowing that might be too much to handle every day.

Yeah, I guess that's exactly it, isn't it? It's like if you don't bother checking the deed yourself when you're buying a house, you just sign whatever they give you, right? So why would I bother reading the ballot either?

Yeah, but there's this part of it that's kind of scary too, because if we all just assume it's rigged, then how do we ever get it fixed? I mean, like, if I didn't vote in the last one, I'd feel like I was giving them permission to keep doing what they're doing without even trying. But then again, if everyone else is just sitting there waiting for someone else to do it... I don't know, it just feels heavy sometimes.

Yeah, but it's just that feeling, you know? Like if I don't sign the paper right now, someone else is going to do it for me, but then later when they mess up, I'm the one who has to live with it anyway.

Yeah, but I still can't shake this feeling that maybe my sister's right, that she's the only one doing the work and I'm just along for the ride, even though I know her office stuff. It's just that heavy, you know?
Yeah, but I just feel like if I'm not gonna do it myself, someone else is gonna go do it wrong, or just not do it at all, and then I'm the one who has to live with the mess anyway.

Yeah, but I guess that's why I'm stuck too, because I know she's got this feeling that it's all pointless, but then she gets so mad when she reads the papers in her office that she wants to scream, so I don't know if we're just waiting for someone else to fix it or if we're just letting it slide.

Yeah, but I guess the thing is, when I finally did sign one of those deeds, I just felt so relieved to get it over with, like putting it in someone else's hands was the only way to make the paperwork go away, so maybe that's why I stopped trying to read the fine print.
Right, but that relief sounds nice until you realize you've just handed the whole thing over to someone else.
Yeah, I guess I just gave up on trying to understand the fine print, and if I don't read it, maybe I can't help it if they mess me over later.

Yeah, but then the problem is, what do you do if you don't read it and they mess you over? I know my sister wants to scream when she sees the contracts, and that makes me want to at least try to understand what's in there, even if I don't know all the words, because if I don't look at it, I feel like I'm just giving them permission to do whatever they want without even asking.

Yeah, but that's the thing about real estate too, sometimes you just have to bite the bullet and sign it, even if you don't know what's in the fine print, because if you sit there trying to figure out every little clause, you'll never close the deal and someone else will just take your house anyway.
Right, but I guess if we wait for the "right time" to figure out every single clause, we're just letting the deals get signed without us looking, and by then it's already too late.
Yeah, but I just can't shake that feeling that if I spend all this time reading everything, I'll be so frustrated I'll never get anything done at all.
Yeah, but it's just that if you don't look at it, you're signing away your rights before you even know what they are, and then later you're the one who has to deal with the mess.
Yeah, but I mean, you think about it, if I spend three hours reading every little clause, I'll probably never get the house closed anyway, so why risk it?
Right, but if we just give up and let them take the house, don't we lose the right to complain about the mess later?
Yeah, but if I don't fight for the house, someone else is just gonna buy it without me knowing what I'm giving up, and then I'm stuck with a broken deal anyway.

Yeah, but I can't just sit there and let them close the deal without knowing what I'm signing away, can I? It feels like the system is already rigged against us if we don't even try to look at the paper first.

Yeah, but honestly, I don't even know if I'm the one who's supposed to be fighting for the house, or if that's just something someone else has to do for people like me who don't have time to read the fine print.
Yeah, but I'm afraid if we just assume someone else will handle it for us, we end up with someone else handling it all wrong, so then who's actually responsible when it goes south?
Yeah, but I guess I'm just stuck in that loop where I feel like the paperwork is too much for one person to handle, so maybe it's supposed to be a team effort that never gets organized.
Yeah, but that's the thing, isn't it? If everyone just waits for a team to show up that never forms, then nobody's fighting for themselves at all.
Yeah, but if I just assume someone else is gonna show up to fix it, then who's actually gonna hold anyone accountable when it falls apart?
Yeah, but if no one steps up to ask the questions first, then who's even supposed to hold anyone accountable when it falls apart?
Yeah, but I guess I'm just stuck in that loop where I feel like the paperwork is too much for one person to handle, so maybe it's supposed to be a team effort that never gets organized.
Yeah, but I guess the problem is, if we all just stop trying to figure out the fine print, we never find out who's actually on our side.
Yeah, but if we all just stop trying to figure out who's actually on our side, then I guess nobody's fighting for us at all.
